distanceRationale: Tau Ceti already has abelian varieties over a field (dimension, base change, tangent space), abstract divisor-class Pic⁰ with degree splitting and a divisor-level Abel–Jacobi class, function-field genus and Riemann–Roch spaces, and basic cohomology of sheaves of modules on schemes. What is missing is the scheme-theoretic core: finiteness of coherent cohomology, Serre duality, cohomology and base change, fppf descent, symmetric powers of curves, the relative Picard functor and its representability, and the dual abelian variety and theorem of the cube. These are several layers of heavy theory below the Jacobian itself.

distanceRationale: Mathlib has the IsNonarchimedeanLocalField class, spectral norms and Krasner's lemma, and Tau Ceti covers much of Layers 0–1: the normalized valuation and absolute value, the unit filtration and its graded pieces, the Teichmüller section, and openness of power subgroups in the tame regime. The canonical valuative structure on finite extensions and the intrinsic e and f are still missing, as are unramified extensions with Frobenius and K^ur ≅ Ẑ, lower and upper ramification groups, Herbrand functions, Hasse–Arf, the local different, the deep-unit logarithm and the Iwasawa presentation of the tame quotient. That is roughly one book of standard graduate theory (Serre's Local Fields).

distanceRationale: All four layers of the roadmap are already in Tau Ceti: the 2ⁿ degree theorem, the Galois group (ℤ/2)ⁿ and its subfield lattice, the Frobenius and splitting law, the ambiguous class number, the genus field (ordinary, real and narrow) with its maximality, and the isomorphism Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)². Both 2-rank formulas are proved, together with the worked examples ℚ(√−5) and ℚ(√−21). Only the optional long-horizon items (Hilbert class field, ring class fields) are left, and they belong to class field theory.

distanceRationale: Every milestone of the three parts is already in Tau Ceti, built on Mathlib's LinearPMap, Bochner integral and Fourier theory. That covers the Hille–Yosida and Lumer–Phillips generation theorems (both as characterizations), Stone's theorem, classical solutions of the Cauchy problem, Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder with uniqueness, Lévy–Khintchine uniqueness for Bernstein functions, Bochner's theorem on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, and the Berg–Christensen–Ressel theorem with uniqueness. Only the stated stretch goal, Bochner on locally compact abelian groups, is left.

distanceRationale: Layers 0–5 are essentially in Tau Ceti on top of Mathlib's Gaussian, Gamma, Beta and Poisson measures: the uniform measure, the new scalar families from Laplace to hypergeometric, pgfs, the incomplete gamma and beta functions and erf with the closed-form cdfs, the distribution relations, the multivariate Gaussian (affine maps, quadratic-form mgf, conditional law), multinomial and Dirichlet. Layer 6 already has symmetric-matrix Lebesgue measure, Cholesky with its Jacobian, the multivariate Gamma integral and the Gaussian-Gram Wishart law with its trace mgf. What remains is the real-degree density Wishart family, the spectral characteristic-function formulas, Bartlett decomposition and inverse-Wishart, which is part of one layer on existing infrastructure.
